verified_claims: OS Terrain 50 is published as grid and contour data in multiple formats.
The grid supply uses a 50m grid in ASCII and GML 3.2.1 simple-features form.
Grid and contour products are supplied separately in compressed geographic tile folders.
ASCII grid data is supplied alongside GML grid data.
Per-tile metadata includes the 10km National Grid tile reference.
Per-tile metadata includes spatial and temporal extent information.
Terrain feature identifiers use the pattern os.t50, tile name and a sequential number.
GML geometries identify British National Grid through the EPSG reference system.
Tile identity and feature identity must both be retained when joining a cell sample to evidence.
A product-level specification does not prove that a particular TQ29 binary was downloaded.
Grid sample promotion requires exact row and column indexing against the supplied tile origin and spacing.
Contour and spot-height features are not interchangeable with a candidate-specific raster cell sample.
A refreshed tile can change feature lifecycle evidence, so current bytes and checksum must be retained.
No official TQ29 binary checksum or two candidate cell height values have been read back.
